top_choice_rationale: P002 is the original, experimentally verified discovery with a short documentable chain: the 2011 Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction of flat bands at the magic angle, then the 2018 Jarillo-Herrero group observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle, since reproduced by independent groups with transport, scanning probes and spectroscopy. A citation limited to the predicted bands and observed phases is silent on the still-open pairing mechanism, so the maturity concern does not bear on it. I accept the attribution weakness (Cao and the early experimental groups cannot be named) and rank P001 a close second: it is mature and cleanly attributed, though I still want to know what Ye added that was first and not only better. P003 ranks third as a secure diffuse-flux discovery whose credit allocation I cannot fully verify, and no award is last because every proposal rewards a verified result.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for the credited people on P001, P002 and P003; my field of electron microscopy is adjacent to the moire-materials characterisation literature but I have no tie to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer, and Johansson is a Chalmers colleague without a stake in these proposals
